skeleton: The data carries a recession-signal shape: {regime_count} regime change{regime_plural} alongside {anomaly_count} indicator surprise{anomaly_plural}. Leading indicators preceded coincident ones, which is the canonical pre-contraction sequence — though false positives are documented and the actual decision should weight cross-indicator agreement, not any single series. The forecast horizon is reliable for nowcasting but degrades quickly past 2-3 months.

Indicators are tracking a stable expansion regime: {motif_label} captures the dominant dynamic with no regime break detected. In macroeconomics terms, this is the 'middle of the cycle' — the part where leading indicators stay roughly co-moving and policy transmission lags are predictable.

Aurora surfaced anomalies in the rate / yield-curve series. Term-structure inversions have preceded most US recessions in the last half-century with a 6-18 month lead time, but they're not deterministic — the standard caveat is that the modern policy regime, with active QT/QE, may have shifted the relationship. Use these as one input alongside leading-indicator dispersion, not as a standalone signal.
